subject: Pricing components: hosted baseline vs reserved and private packaging
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing components: hosted baseline vs reserved and private packaging

Tom — thanks for the rate card request. Attached is a short worksheet showing the three deployment primitives you asked about (hosted API baseline, reserved/dedicated capacity, and private on-prem). I wanted to call out the key building blocks so the procurement team can see what moves vs what is fixed: 

• Hosted baseline (no commit): per-token generation fee, per-embedding unit, plus optional add-ons (observability retention, higher concurrent streams). Example list rates in the attachment: $0.0035 per 1k generation tokens; embeddings $0.00075 per vector unit.

• Dedicated / Reserved: monthly committed pool (GPU-hours) + discounted per-token effective rate when amortized. Typical structure we propose: a monthly commit for 12 months, which reduces effective token cost by ~40–55% depending on commit size. Upfront: contract and onboarding fees may apply.

• Private / On-prem: platform license + support fee + infra (customer-managed GPUs). Typical: platform fee (e.g., $25k/mo) + deployment services (one-time) + optional premium SLA. Per-token economics are highly contingent on hardware and utilization.

I put three illustrative scenarios in the sheet using your volume guidance from discovery (avg 2B tokens/mo with spikes to 6B): baseline hosted for month 1–3, transition to 12mo reserved starting month 4, and an optional private pilot timeline. The worksheet shows the blended effective per-token cost and the delta vs pure hosted.

Key negotiation levers I recommend we highlight to Acme: commitment length (6 vs 12 vs 24 months), committed throughput (which affects effective token rate), early-transition credits (apply remaining hosted credits toward first reserved month), and observability/add-on bundling (we can include 30 days of extended metrics retention as part of a pilot).

I attached the acme_rate_request.xlsx with the numbers and a concise cheat sheet (redwood_pricing_cheatsheet_v3.pdf). If procurement wants a formal redline or a single-page headcount-friendly summary, I can produce it next.

Thanks — Steph
--

Thanks Steph — useful start. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) Can you show a concrete example that compares: (A) 3 months hosted at expected usage, (B) immediate 12mo reserved commit, (C) hosted for 3 months then convert to 12mo reserved? We want month-by-month cashflow and the effective per-token numbers.
2) For private: what are the typical one-time deployment fees and timeline (we have security requirements — SOC2 & VPC) and how does that change the unit economics?
3) Discounts: our procurement target is a 20% off list for the first 6 months on hosted, and a further 10–20% uplift on any committed reserved pricing. Is that in the realm of possibility?

Also looped Sarah (SaaSOps) and procurement for the terms discussion.

—Tom

Subject: Re: Pricing components: hosted baseline vs reserved and private packaging

Tom / Sarah / procurement team — thanks for the questions, see answers inline and in attached updated worksheet (tab: month_by_month). High-level summary first, then the month-by-month cashflow you asked for.

Summary answers:
• Hosted 3mo vs immediate 12mo reserved vs staged (3mo hosted -> 12mo reserved): for your 2B avg / 6B peak profile we model the following illustrative effective costs (numbers are illustrative and in the sheet):
  - Pure hosted (no commit): effective blended cost ~ $0.0035 per 1k gen tokens (list); monthly cost ~ $7,000 for 2B tokens (note these numbers are normalized per 1k tokens in the sheet).
  - Immediate 12mo reserved: assume 50% discount on list after amortizing monthly platform/commit fees -> effective ~ $0.0018 per 1k tokens (savings driven by steady utilization).
  - Staged (hosted 3mo then reserve): higher first-quarter cost (hosted); amortized reserved saves start month 4 and total 12-mo TCO generally sits between the two depending on timing of spikes. The worksheet shows month-by-month cashflows and a two-year blended view.

• Private / On-prem: one-time deployment professional services typically range $60–120k depending on network/VPC work and integration. Platform fee commonly starts at $25k/mo for the private control plane + support. If Acme owns GPUs, the marginal per-token runs close to $0.0009–0.0015 per 1k tokens depending on instance type and utilization. We included a sensitivity table with GPU utilization at 40/60/80% to show unit economics.

• Discounts / negotiation: a concrete commercial proposal we can offer for ACME: 15% off hosted list for first 6 months (instead of 20% requested), with a path to an additional 10–20% off for a signed 12-mo reserved commit (tiered by commit size). Rationale: preserves pricing integrity for hosted customers while giving a clear path to lower unit costs via reservation.

Attached tab "cashflows" shows exactly what you asked. A few operational notes that affect price: KV cache reuse (reduces token counts for repeated prompts), model quantization (reduces GPU hours), and prefix caching for top queries — we can model those into the reserved sizing if you want.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ll produce a clean 1-pager with the month-by-month numbers (for procurement) by EOD tomorrow.
2) If you want to test the reserved economics, we can do a 60-day pilot with a capped commit and a credit applied from hosted spend.
3) Laura (pricing) and Marcus (contracts) will follow up on operational terms and the SOW/DocuSign if we move forward.

Please see the attached updated workbook. Happy to hop on a call to walk through the scenarios.

Thanks — Steph
--
